5. It is contended on behalf of the plaintiff that the agreements were executed one after another with a view to save limitation because of the fact that besides the above suits, there were other litigations pending in different courts over the same property, but this is not a legal ground to drag the matter. There is no doubt that various litigation had cropped up out of the suit property but these litigations did not stand in the way of getting a sale deed. The plaintiff sought specific performance in respect of the fourth agreement executed through his wife as attorney of the defendants. It is an admitted fact that pursuant to the cancellation of the power of attorney dated 29.07.2010; the defendants entered into an agreement with Sakura Saber on 09.05.2012 and with prior approval of the RAJUK, the defendants executed a sale deed on 21.04.2013 in her favour. This purchaser is claiming that she is a bonafide purchaser for value without notice to the previous contract. The trial court rejected the plaint on the reasoning that the suit was barred under section 54A of the Transfer of Property Act, inasmuch as, the plaintiff without depositing the balance consideration amount has instituted the suit.] 

 7. In the first and second agreements there were recitals that after the death of their predecessor, the defendants were in need of money and accordingly they were completed to sell the property. Since 1987 there is nothing on record to infer that the plaintiff fulfilled his part of obligation and it was only on 30th July, 2012, he instituted Title Suit No. 838 of 2012 for specific performance of contract after the cancellation of the power of attorney. He was sleeping over the matter for years together and awaken after such action. Plaintiff claimed that he published a notice on 27.10.2010 in the newspaper cautioning others not to enter into any transaction in respect of the property and that on 02.11.2010 he published another legal notice in the newspaper regarding the cancellation of the power of attorney, which constituted the cause of action for filing the suit for specific performance. So, the purpose for filing the suit was the cancellation of the power of attorney. The limitation for such suit starts from the date of refusal to execute the sale deed. Prior to that date he consumed time without completing the transaction although the first agreement was executed on 07.07.1987.
